name: Smartsheet
verdict: Self-serve after a one-time Developer Tools registration that Smartsheet can deny, in which case you contact your Customer Success Manager. No app review is documented after that; approval time is unknown, likely days.
needGuide: Yes — register for Developer Tools with a service-account user first, then create the app.

auth.detail: Authorization code grant: authorize at app.smartsheet.com/b/authorize, exchange at api.smartsheet.com/2.0/token. Access token lasts about 7 days (604,799 s); each refresh returns a new access and refresh token. Authorization code valid about 10 minutes; HTTPS required. PKCE is not mentioned. Tokens for standard, Smartsheet Regions and Smartsheet Gov are not interchangeable; regional OAuth hosts were not confirmed.

effort.timeToProduction: unknown (registration approval time not documented); likely days

approval.gate: A one-time Developer Tools registration (service-account email + Developer Agreement); Smartsheet can deny it, in which case contact your Customer Success Manager. After that no app review is documented: the 'Publish App?' option only makes the app's profile page public.

scopes.why: 17 scopes (ADMIN_, CREATE_, READ_, WRITE_ and more) that don't override sharing permissions.
scopes.summary: 17 scopes: ADMIN_SHEETS/SIGHTS/USERS/WEBHOOKS/WORKSPACES, CREATE_SHEETS/SIGHTS, DELETE_SHEETS/SIGHTS, READ_CONTACTS/EVENTS/SHEETS/SIGHTS/USERS, SHARE_SHEETS/SIGHTS, WRITE_SHEETS. Scopes do not override user sharing permissions. No scope is documented as triggering review.

cost: Free to register as far as documented; API token generation needs a Business, Enterprise or Advanced Work Management plan; whether Developer Tools needs a paid plan is unconfirmed
prerequisites: Account and owner: Use a dedicated company-owned Smartsheet 'service account' (not a personal account) to register and own the app.

Where you register: Submit the service-account email on the Developer Tools Registration page and accept the Developer Agreement → in Smartsheet open Developer Tools → create developer profile → Create New App (name, description, URL, support contact, redirect URL)
Cost: Free to register as far as documented; API token generation needs a Business, Enterprise or Advanced Work Management plan; whether Developer Tools needs a paid plan is unconfirmed

registerAt.path: Submit the service-account email on the Developer Tools Registration page and accept the Developer Agreement → in Smartsheet open Developer Tools → create developer profile → Create New App (name, description, URL, support contact, redirect URL)

steps.do: Choose or create a company service-account Smartsheet user and register it on the Developer Tools Registration page, accepting the Developer Agreement
After approval, open Developer Tools, create the developer profile, and register the app with redirect URL and support contact
Pick the minimum scopes (e.g. READ_SHEETS, WRITE_SHEETS, READ_USERS) and implement the authorize redirect with a verified state parameter
Exchange the code, store both tokens encrypted, and refresh before the 7-day expiry, saving the new refresh token each time
Test with a second user and, if serving them, EU/AU and Gov accounts separately
Decide whether to flip Publish App? to list the profile publicly

roles.team: Use a dedicated company-owned Smartsheet 'service account' (not a personal account) to register and own the app.
roles.customer: The end user authorizes; scopes never exceed their sharing permissions. ADMIN_* scopes (users, sheets, workspaces, webhooks) likely need an admin user. Customers on EU/AU Regions or Gov need region-specific setup (unconfirmed).

testing: Register and authorize with your own Smartsheet account against your own sheets.
No sandbox or developer-account program was found in the docs fetched.
Test each region separately because tokens are not interchangeable.

blockers.fix: Use a business service-account email and escalate via your Customer Success Manager.

blockers.problem: Regional and Gov tenants use separate environments and tokens
blockers.fix: Confirm host URLs and register per region.
Write the new pair on every refresh, or the user must re-authorize.

blockers.problem: No PKCE documented, so a confidential server-side client is required
blockers.fix: Never ship the secret to a browser.

automation.agentCan: Draft the registration text, write the OAuth and refresh code, handle regional base URLs, and run test calls.
automation.humanMust: Developer Agreement acceptance, service-account sign-in and registration, any CSM escalation, and customer-side consent.

uncertain: Regional (EU/AU/Gov) OAuth hosts, any developer sandbox, the developer-program page (blocked by robots.txt), registration turnaround, and whether a paid plan is needed were not confirmed.
